treaty_name: Convention between the Government of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland and the Government of Canada for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with respect to Taxes on Income and Capital Gains (1978, as amended by Protocols of 1980, 1985, 2003 and 2014)
eif_quote: HMRC DT4600: Statutory Instrument number: SI 1980 No. 709 Entered into force: 17 December 1980 | 2003 Protocol: Statutory Instrument number: SI 2003 No. 2619 Entered into force: 4 May 2004 Has effect: - in Canada from 1 January 2005 | 2014 Protocol: Statutory Instrument number: SI 2014 No. 3274 Entered into force: 18 December 2014 Has effect: - in Canada from 1 January 2015
source_title: gov.uk: Canada-UK Double Taxation Convention 1978 as amended by Protocols of 1980, 1985, 2003 and 2014 (consolidated, in force); gov.uk Canada-UK MLI synthesised text (January 2020)

rates.quote: (a) 5 per cent of the gross amount of the dividends if the beneficial owner is a company which controls, directly or indirectly, at least 10 per cent of the voting power in the company paying the dividends;
(b) 15 per cent of the gross amount of the dividends in all other cases.

2. However, such interest may also be taxed in the Contracting State in which it arises and according to the laws of that State, but if the beneficial owner of the interest is a resident of the other Contracting State, the tax so charged shall not exceed 10 per cent of the gross amount of the interest.

2. However, such royalties may be taxed in the Contracting State in which they arise, and according to the laws of that State, but if the beneficial owner of the royalties is a resident of the other Contracting State, the tax so charged shall not exceed 10 per cent of the gross amount of the royalties.

ppt.quote: The following paragraph 1 of Article 7 of the MLI replaces paragraph 8 of Article 10, paragraph 9 ... | The provisions of the MLI have effect with respect to the Convention: • In the United Kingdom and Canada, for taxes withheld at source, from 1 January 2020; | Notwithstanding any provisions of a Covered Tax Agreement, a benefit under the Covered Tax Agreement shall not be granted in respect of an item of income or capital if it is reasonable to conclude; having regard to all relevant facts and circumstances, that obtaining that benefit was one of the principal purposes of any arrangement or transaction that resulted directly or indirectly in that benefit, unless it is established that granting that benefit in these circumstances would be in accordance with the object and purpose of the relevant provisions of the Covered Tax Agreement.

notes: 5% tier threshold is 10% of the VOTING POWER, recorded as ownership_threshold. MLI Art. 8 not applicable: UK reserved the entirety of Art. 8. MLI Art. 7(1) replaces the treaty main-purpose rules in Arts. 10(8), 11(9), 12(8) from 2020-01-01. valid_from uses Canadian effective dates (UK: 2003 Protocol from 1/6 April 2005; 2014 Protocol from 1 April 2015 for CT/withholding). Royalty valid_from = 2014 Protocol effect (current Art. 12 wording); the 10% cap itself dates from the original Convention. Not modelled: Art. 10(3) exemption for dividends to recognized pension organisations (<=10% holding); Art. 11(3)(c) arm’s-length interest exempt at source ("(c) interest arising in a Contracting State and paid to a resident of the other Contracting State shall not be taxable in the first-mentioned State if the beneficial owner of the interest is a resident of the other Contracting State and is dealing at arm's length with the payer."), except participating interest (11(4)); EDC/UKECGD loans; Art. 12(3): copyright (excl. film/TV), patent/know-how (excl. rental/franchise) and computer software royalties taxable only in residence State.
